title: Half mirror
summary: Split a violet beam equally between the Through and Up detectors with a thin metal film. Its wavelength is 0.38 micrometres. You may place one slab of gold, silver or aluminium in the marked region. The split must be 50/50 within 5 percentage points. The score compares each detector's power with the half it should get and counts the smaller of the two. Light that the metal absorbs lowers it.
hints: Thick metal reflects almost all of the light. A film only a few hundredths of a micrometre thick lets part of it through.
Turn the film by 45 degrees so that the reflected light goes up. Every metal absorbs some light, and at this wavelength silver absorbs the least.
Use silver about 0.023 micrometres thick. If Through gets more than Up, make the film a little thicker; if Up gets more, make it thinner. Turning the film by a degree or two also shifts the balance.

goal.text: Split the beam 50/50 between Through and Up
